summary: Pulaski County, VA tower on Peaks Knob, reported arriving in 1938 (35 ft, glass cab); staffing and vandalism reports to 1964; FFLA lists it standing; no current condition or access found.

facts.design: 35-foot tower with a glass enclosure about seven feet square at the top (1938 newspaper)
facts.status_note: Listed as standing by FFLA; no description of its condition after 1964 found

access.note: 1953 warden posting required permission and an adult leader for groups; no current access information found

events.note: Tower reported arriving from Chicago and being taken to the mountain in February 1938; operation hoped for by March 15
Announced that an observer was to be stationed in the tower during dry seasons, 8 a.m. to sundown; this is the first staffing mention, and it is a plan rather than a confirmed record
Three juveniles arraigned for breaking into and damaging the tower; property destroyed
Telephone line completed to the tower; forest warden David Warden on duty March 1 to mid-May
Lookout David T. Warden, cut off from telephone service, estimated 500 to 600 acres burned
Six windows shot out, landing platform torn away, cistern lock broken; property posted and visitors required to obtain permission
Tower announced as manned for the first time that season; Bobby Long to be on duty until late May, depending on weather (March 13, 1964 notice)

FFLA lists the tower as standing, with coordinates and county

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The name is spelled Peaks Knob (FFLA list and Forest Lookouts header), Peak Knob (page title) and Peak knob (1938-1964 clippings). Treated as one tower in Pulaski County.

notes_for_editor: History is documented through 1964 by newspaper clippings quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; nothing later was found. Height comes from a 1938 newspaper (35 ft = 10.7 m) and is not in the record. Staffing after 1964, current condition and current access are unknown. The 1939 'staffed_first' entry is a planned observer, not a confirmed staffing. Not in the NHLR or FFLOS Virginia listings in the local crawl. Two web searches used.
